rationale: The earlier legitimate call rested almost entirely on the recurring look of the $30.02 amount: three prior charges of exactly the same value (3342487, 3381749, 3545489) on a card whose spend is 87% online. The customer_validation reply removes that explanation: the cardholder denies all four $30.02 charges, states they hold no subscription or service billing that amount, and confirms nobody else has access to the card or account. The recurrence signal itself was already weak (gaps of 13 and 56 days, looks_monthly = false), so with no matching subscription the repeated identical amounts read instead as a card number being milked in small, low-scoring increments (flagged txn risk 0.28, amount 0.45x the card mean). No rare device or region link supports escalation: the flagged device string 'unknown | unknown | unknown | unknown' is a generic placeholder also present in this card's own 180d history, and region 203's newcomer fraud rate (0.14 over 7 cards) is statistically indistinguishable from the 0.10 base rate. Exposure is $120.08 across four charges, so this is a case and a block, not a regulatory filing.
